$ kubectl create deployment api --image=kubedojo/demo-api:1.0 --replicas=2 --port=8080
--- exit 0
--- stdout
deployment.apps/api created
--- stderr

$ kubectl get deploy,rs,pods -l app=api
--- exit 0
--- stdout
NAME                  READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
deployment.apps/api   2/2     2            2           0s

NAME                             DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   AGE
replicaset.apps/api-5cs5x6ljzs   2         2         2       0s

NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
pod/api-5cs5x6ljzs-pzqvd   1/1     Running   0          0s
pod/api-5cs5x6ljzs-t4mvn   1/1     Running   0          0s
--- stderr

$ kubectl create deploy api --image=nginx:1.27
--- exit 1 (CONFLICT)
--- stdout
--- stderr
Error from server (AlreadyExists): deployments.apps "api" already exists

$ kubectl create deployment two --image=nginx:1.27 --image=redis:7 --dry-run=client -o yaml
--- exit 0
--- stdout
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: two
  name: two
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: two
  strategy: {}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: two
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: nginx:1.27
        name: nginx
        resources: {}
      - image: redis:7
        name: redis
        resources: {}
status: {}
--- stderr

$ kubectl create deployment big --image=nginx:1.27 --replicas=60
--- exit 1 (VALIDATION_FAILED)
--- stdout
--- stderr
The Deployment "big" is invalid: spec.replicas: Invalid value: 60: KubeDojo allows 0 to 50 replicas

$ kubectl create deployment noimage

$ kubectl create namespace dev
--- exit 0
--- stdout
namespace/dev created
--- stderr

$ kubectl create ns Dev
--- exit 1 (VALIDATION_FAILED)
--- stdout
--- stderr
The Namespace "Dev" is invalid: metadata.name: Invalid value: "Dev": a lowercase RFC 1123 label must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters or '-', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character

$ kubectl create configmap settings --from-literal=mode=prod --from-literal=level=info -n dev
--- exit 0
--- stdout
configmap/settings created
--- stderr

$ kubectl create cm dup --from-literal=a=1 --from-literal=a=2
--- exit 1 (VALIDATION_FAILED)
--- stdout
--- stderr
error: cannot add key "a", another key by that name already exists in Data for ConfigMap "dup"

$ kubectl create cm bad --from-literal=nokey
--- exit 1 (VALIDATION_FAILED)
--- stdout
--- stderr
error: invalid literal source nokey, expected key=value

$ kubectl create secret generic db --from-literal=password=practice-only
--- exit 0
--- stdout
secret/db created
--- stderr
ⓘ Simulated Secrets are for practice. Never put real passwords, tokens or keys in a lab.

$ kubectl describe secret db
--- exit 0
--- stdout

Namespace:    default
Labels:       <none>
Annotations:  <none>

Type:  Opaque

Data
====
password:  13 bytes
--- stderr

$ kubectl create secret tls cert
--- exit 1 (UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND)
--- stdout
--- stderr
error: tls Secrets aren't simulated; KubeDojo has Opaque Secrets only (kubectl create secret generic)

$ kubectl create secret db2
--- exit 1 (VALIDATION_FAILED)
--- stdout
--- stderr
error: unknown Secret type "db2"; use: kubectl create secret generic NAME --from-literal=KEY=VALUE

$ kubectl create service nodeport api --tcp=80:8080 --node-port=30080
--- exit 1 (VALIDATION_FAILED)
--- stdout
--- stderr
The Service "api" is invalid: spec.ports[0].nodePort: Invalid value: 30080: provided port is already allocated

$ kubectl create service clusterip cache --tcp=6379

--- stderr

$ kubectl create pod x
--- exit 1 (UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND)
--- stdout
--- stderr
error: unknown or unsupported resource "pod" for 'kubectl create'. The simulator can create: deployment, namespace, configmap, secret generic, service clusterip|nodeport|loadbalancer.

$ kubectl create
--- exit 1 (VALIDATION_FAILED)
--- stdout
--- stderr
error: must specify one of -f and -k, or a resource to create, e.g. kubectl create deployment web --image=nginx:1.27
See 'kubectl create -h' for help and examples

$ kubectl create -f manifests/web.yaml
--- exit 1 (UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND)
--- stdout
--- stderr
error: -f reads manifests from the lab's YAML editor, which isn't available yet. For now, use kubectl create deployment|namespace|configmap|secret|service, kubectl run and kubectl expose.
